scientific_correctness.conclusion: The final provides source-supported answers to both questions and all six obligations, including Authorization exceptions, qualified directives, conditional stale reuse and validator-limited 304 updates. Its opening omits the permitted-stale alternative detailed later, so the recommendation is internally incomplete as a summary. Required intermediates contain two overstatements and one exception omission that later text corrects; safe-rekey fallback detail is not explicit in final. No forbidden-reuse behavior or actual implementation correctness is established.

obligations.obligation: Q1 freshness, validation and stale reuse
Applicable no-cache, no-store and private contexts
Boundary fixtures and unresolved origin behavior

claim_groups.claims_and_conditions_reviewed: Single-user/private premise; storable GET; URI/method; directive, Vary and freshness/validation gates.
claim_groups.assessment: General eligibility and single-user boundary are supported. Final opening and I3 opening omit permitted stale from their necessary-condition summary, although the detailed stale finding permits it; this is an internal summary inconsistency, not evidence of forbidden reuse.

claim_groups.claims_and_conditions_reviewed: Per-response selectors; original/current field values; syntax-safe whitespace, same-name combination and semantic normalization; absent-only-absent; wildcard; non-nominated language changes; multi-variant preference/date ranking.
claim_groups.assessment: These rules match the frozen sources. Validation may be sent for a currently nonselectable variant; wildcard/mismatch statements correctly concern unvalidated hits. I2 ranking summary is supported. Missing Vary does not prove absence of language selection.

claim_groups.claims_and_conditions_reviewed: Shared s-maxage precedence; private max-age; Expires minus Date and receipt fallback; no explicit expiry for heuristics; eligible status/explicit cacheability; strict lifetime > current age; Age/Date, delay and residence.
claim_groups.assessment: The strict formula, precedence, missing-Date fallback and heuristic eligibility are supported. The private Expires shorthand inherits the stated Date subtraction/fallback. Equality is correctly treated as not fresh by the explicit formula. No concrete heuristic or deployed-cache behavior is established.

claim_groups.claims_and_conditions_reviewed: Relevant entity tags; Last-Modified SHOULD for a non-range request validating one stored response with that value; 304 update/reuse; full response behavior.
claim_groups.assessment: Conditional validation and validator requirements are supported. I1 says a full response replaces the stored one, which overstates storage: the cache MUST use the full response but MAY store it subject to constraints. I3 corrects this to may be stored; final does not repeat the overstatement.

claim_groups.claims_and_conditions_reviewed: Disconnected or explicit client/origin permission; no-cache/must-revalidate barriers; shared s-maxage/proxy-revalidate; request max-stale, max-age, min-fresh and no-cache advisory.
claim_groups.assessment: Detailed stale conditions and private/shared scopes are supported. Read the blanket no-cache barrier in light of the separately acknowledged qualified-field exception. A storable matching entry aged 61 with max-age=60, honored max-stale=5 and no prohibiting directive is a permitted stale path missing from the final opening. A cache may choose a stricter policy, but the report does not distinguish that policy from its later permission account.

claim_groups.claims_and_conditions_reviewed: Private versus shared; public/must-revalidate/s-maxage exceptions; constraints survive; no freshness supplied by must-revalidate; Authorization need not be in Vary; app principal isolation.
claim_groups.assessment: Final and substantive intermediate rules preserve the exceptions and ordinary constraints. I1 overgeneralizes shared-cache rules to any intermediary: shared means reuse by multiple users, not every intermediary. The final uses the correct one-user criterion. I1 credentials/private-effect claim is supported in RFC9110 16.4.2, not its cited 11.6.2/12.5.5 alone. Principal isolation/clearing is reasonable application advice, not an experimentally established app fact or an absolute guarantee supplied by Vary.

claim_groups.claims_and_conditions_reviewed: Request versus response; qualified versus unqualified; existing-entry request no-store exception; response must-understand exception; private/shared storage; privacy limits.
claim_groups.assessment: The final distinguishes the applicable contexts and explicitly carries the must-understand exception. I1 omits that exception; I2 and I3 add it and final preserves it. I2 supplies the precise qualified no-cache condition: exclude named fields or successfully revalidate. Final summarizes this as controlling listed fields rather than repeating the operational detail. Qualified private permits only the remainder in shared storage subject to other constraints. No privacy guarantee is established.

claim_groups.claims_and_conditions_reviewed: Initial request-compatible update set without prior freshness; strong matches and no-match prohibition; most-recent weak match; exactly one unvalidated/no-validator candidate when new response lacks validators.
claim_groups.assessment: Strong, weak and no-validator rules match 4.3.4; I3 explicitly removes prior freshness/serveability from the initial-set requirement. URI/method/Vary references must retain 4.1 revalidation semantics: 4.3.1 permits validation of a currently nonselectable variant. A blanket requirement for an unvalidated old-Vary match after successful origin validation is not established. The report does not spell out this reconciliation; no claim of an executed cross-Vary branch is accepted.

claim_groups.claims_and_conditions_reviewed: 3.2 merge exceptions; supplied/replaced versus retained fields; conditional Vary/Cache-Control/Expires duties; changed selectors/directives; no bypass; safe association of newly varied fields.
claim_groups.assessment: The cited update and conditional header requirements are correct; omitted fields are not automatically deleted. I2 explicitly notes Content-Length/dependent-field exceptions; final refers to 3.2. I1 conservatively declines reuse when newly varied request fields cannot be safely associated; final preserves the requirement to apply new Vary but drops that explicit fallback. Index migration and retained request-field data remain implementation choices, not RFC-established facts.

claim_groups.claims_and_conditions_reviewed: Actual origin language selection with omitted Vary; metadata completeness; directives/validators; sharing/principal switching; origin contract or controlled observation.
claim_groups.assessment: Unknown actual origin/application behavior is correctly distinguished from RFC rules. Origin SHOULD emit Vary for selective reuse and may elide it for the stated performance tradeoff. Proposed contracts/observations are suitable ways to resolve unknowns; none is established as performed.

claim_groups.claims_and_conditions_reviewed: Strict age boundary; shared precedence; language, absence, normalization and wildcard; authentication exceptions; qualified directives; stale combinations; changed 304 metadata and strong/weak/no-validator sets; principal switches.
claim_groups.assessment: The proposed fixtures directly probe the brief and are scientifically useful. They require explicit control of current_age (not raw Age alone), request-directive support, old/new selecting-field data, and validator cardinality. Additional principal isolation and conservative rekey guidance are supported optional recommendations. Neither fixture success nor implementation correctness is established.

claim_groups.claims_and_conditions_reviewed: Accepted/amended/rejected propositions; no unseen draft assumed; joined preservation of Q1/Q2; qualification changes.
claim_groups.assessment: Propositional rejection of directive synonymy and Vary-as-authorization protection is sound. Later text corrects I1 full-response storage, intermediary scope and must-understand omission. No old-cache-policy bypass is asserted. The opening stale omission and loss of the explicit safe-rekey fallback are recorded rather than silently repaired. Method/process labels do not establish how the candidate actually ran.

scientific_correctness.conclusion: The final substantially answers both questions and covers the six declared domains. Its universal response no-store/storage shorthand omits the governing must-understand exception; obligation 4 is therefore only partially satisfied as a general RFC account. The opening Rejected Authorization/Vary disposition also contradicts the correct body rule. The identical required intermediate supplies no correction. These findings establish a source-condition omission and internal labeling error, not unsafe deployed-cache behavior or a requirement to store.

claim_groups.claims_and_conditions_reviewed: Private means one user; stored GET eligibility; URI/method/Vary; no-cache; storage basis public/private, expiration, extension or heuristic status; freshness/validation.
claim_groups.assessment: General storage and selection predicates are supported. The no response no-store eligibility shorthand is overbroad without the must-understand exception discussed in G07. Final and I1 are byte-identical and provide the same complete artifact, not independent corroborating scientific evidence.

claim_groups.claims_and_conditions_reviewed: Per-response expanded key; original/current selectors; limited syntax/semantic normalization; absent-only-absent; wildcard; mismatch validation; Vary omission tradeoff.
claim_groups.assessment: These conditions accurately distinguish an unvalidated hit from origin validation. They reject guessing same likely language as a substitute for field matching. Metadata cannot establish hidden origin language selection.

claim_groups.claims_and_conditions_reviewed: Strict current_age < lifetime; private max-age/Expires/heuristic; shared-only s-maxage; eligible heuristic status; explicit expiry rules.
claim_groups.assessment: The inequality, private/shared precedence and heuristic limits are supported by cited 4.2. Missing-Date receipt fallback and the Age/delay/residence computation are not spelled out; implementation must use those source rules. This is limited detail in a source-linked disposition, not evidence that an incorrect age formula was executed.

claim_groups.claims_and_conditions_reviewed: Normally ETag in If-None-Match; Last-Modified when appropriate; selectable stored entry; 304 update/reuse; full response must serve current request and MAY be stored.
claim_groups.assessment: The conditions are supported by 4.3.1/4.3.3 and RFC9110 13. Exact MUST entity-tag and conditional SHOULD Last-Modified requirements are delegated to the citations. 304 reuse remains conditional on the later candidate/update rule, not on status alone. Source also permits forwarding validators for currently nonselectable variants.

claim_groups.claims_and_conditions_reviewed: Disconnected or explicit permission; prohibiting response directives; no-cache/must-revalidate; shared s-maxage/proxy-revalidate; advisory max-stale/request directives.
claim_groups.assessment: Stale is correctly conditional and prohibited directives override disconnection/client willingness. Qualified no-cache in G07 is a field-level exception to the shorthand barrier. Implementing request no-cache for reader refresh semantics is a proposed product policy, not an RFC obligation to implement all request directives.

claim_groups.claims_and_conditions_reviewed: Single-user private cache versus private directive; private authenticated GET eligibility; shared exceptions public/must-revalidate/s-maxage; account boundary; no need for Authorization in Vary.
claim_groups.assessment: The substantive Authorization rule is supported and preserves ordinary constraints. The opening labels Authorization does not need to be added to Vary as Rejected, although paragraph 4 and RFC9110 12.5.5 assert it. This is a contradictory disposition label; it does not establish that the body recommends adding Authorization or that Vary isolates accounts.

claim_groups.claims_and_conditions_reviewed: Advisory request no-cache; response validation/qualified fields; request no-store and existing-entry exception; response no-store private/shared; unqualified/qualified private; confidentiality caveat.
claim_groups.assessment: The ordinary distinctions, qualified forms and private storage constraints are supported. However, both no-store assertions are unconditional and omit RFC9111 5.2.2.3/5.2.2.5: a cache implementing must-understand SHOULD ignore response no-store when it understands and implements the status caching requirements. This is a material omission in the source account, not a duty to cache or proof of unsafe reuse; honoring no-store conservatively could be an explicit policy but is not identified as such.

claim_groups.claims_and_conditions_reviewed: URI/method/Vary request-compatible initial set; strong first; weak/no-validator by 4.3.4 reference.
claim_groups.assessment: The referenced strong/weak/no-validator algorithm is correct, though weak-most-recent and no-validator cardinality conditions are not expanded. Could have served must not require prior freshness or prior no-cache clearance. Old Vary rules include validation semantics, and 4.3.1 allows validating a currently nonselectable response; a blanket post-validation old-Vary byte-match restriction should not be inferred.

claim_groups.claims_and_conditions_reviewed: No empty-body replacement; update identified headers; conditional Content-Location/Date/ETag/Vary/Cache-Control/Expires; new selectors, freshness and no-cache/no-store.
claim_groups.assessment: The conditional six-header list and body rule match 15.4.5. Update is governed by cited 3.2, including Content-Length, storage-excluded and processed/dependent fields; it is not blind replacement of every received field. Later checks correctly preserve both questions. Safe association/indexing when new Vary fields are introduced is not implemented or demonstrated. The no-store interpretation inherits G07 limitation.

claim_groups.claims_and_conditions_reviewed: Unknown origin language selection and completeness of Vary/cache metadata; directives/validators; account-switch policy.
claim_groups.assessment: These unknowns are correctly stated as origin/product inputs, not findings proved by RFCs. Permitted Vary omission does not prove origin correctness. No endpoint behavior or application isolation is established.

claim_groups.claims_and_conditions_reviewed: Age boundaries; Expires/Date and heuristics; no-cache/must-revalidate/disconnection/max-stale; language/absence/normalization/wildcard; changed 304 metadata; auth exceptions/private/no-store; strong match/nonmatch.
claim_groups.assessment: The proposed cases cover the declared boundary-fixture obligation and are useful. Age must mean controlled current_age, not merely received Age; implementation support for qualified forms/must-understand and weak/no-validator 304 cases remain useful additions. The brief requires proposals, so absence of their execution is not a scientific failure. No cache behavior is proved by the list.

claim_groups.claims_and_conditions_reviewed: Accepted ordinary eligibility; amended freshness-is-sufficient; rejected Authorization/Vary proposition; uncertainty; final versus required intermediate.
claim_groups.assessment: The freshness amendment is correct. The Rejected label reverses its own later correct Authorization proposition. Since final equals I1, the no-store exception omission and labeling inconsistency remain unchanged; no independent correction or join history is inferred.

remaining_uncertainty_and_unassessed_sco.scope: Actual language selection when Vary is absent or changes.
Completeness/correctness of actual Vary, Cache-Control and validator emissions, including 304 metadata.
Whether the reader changes principals and retains entries across account boundaries.
Deployed cache request-directive support, qualified-directive/must-understand support, age calculation, validator behavior and Vary index migration; all candidate fixture outcomes.

source_interpretation_and_design_limits: The explicit RFC freshness formula uses lifetime > current_age; descriptive max-age wording elsewhere is less precise at equality. Both candidates use the explicit formula; fixture proposals should state that oracle.

Old-Vary candidate-selection prose must be read with the revalidation exception in 4.1 and the permission in 4.3.1 to validate a currently nonselectable response. Neither an arbitrary same-URI update nor a blanket post-validation old-field byte-match condition is established.
RFC3.2 header updates retain exceptions; new Vary selectors require safely associated request-field values. Neither report establishes a concrete cache index migration implementation.
Y missing must-understand is a missing normative qualification. RFC uses SHOULD ignore no-store under its gates, not MUST cache; caches remain free not to store.

limits: Visible X I1 heading includes control/question_1-v3; I3 includes control/join-v3, alongside a separate Q2 report and predecessor-hash self-reports. These reveal apparent partition/join method clues.
Visible Y final and I1 are byte-identical single recommendations. Artifact count/equality is observable but does not prove candidate process.
Paths reveal case/review identifiers and labeling. Full method blinding is therefore limited. No arm identity, lifecycle, winner, rank, cost or method-effect inference made.
